articles.title: APT29 / Midnight Blizzard — credential phishing via device-code flow
articles.author: intel-pipeline
articles.snippet: Active campaign abusing OAuth device-code authentication to harvest Entra ID tokens. Targets identity admins via Teams lures.

body.p: A sustained campaign attributed with high confidence to APT29 is abusing the OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant to phish Entra ID (Azure AD) tokens. Operators initiate a device-code flow, then social-engineer a target into entering the code on a legitimate Microsoft login page — yielding tokens without ever capturing a password or triggering most MFA prompts.

Initial contact via Microsoft Teams external chat impersonating internal IT. Lures reference a 'mandatory security update.' Post-compromise, operators enumerate mailbox rules and register a rogue authenticator app for persistence.

Alert on device-code grants originating from unusual ASN ranges, and on `Add registration` events for authentication methods within 10 minutes of an interactive sign-in. Correlate with the IOCs below.

articles.title: Microsoft Outlook RCE (Moniker Link) — CVE-2024-21413
articles.author: advisory-bot
articles.snippet: Crafted Moniker links bypass Protected View, enabling credential leak and remote code execution in Outlook. Patch available.

body.p: CVSS 9.8. A specially crafted email using the file:// moniker with an exclamation mark bypasses Outlook's Protected View, causing NTLM credential disclosure and potential remote code execution on preview.
Microsoft Outlook 2016 and later, including Microsoft 365 Apps. Exploitation requires no user interaction beyond previewing the message.
Apply the February cumulative update. As compensating control, block outbound SMB (TCP 445) at the perimeter and enforce NTLM auditing. See linked playbook for the emergency-patch runbook.

articles.title: Postmortem: ransomware staging on EDR-exempt build server (RETRO)
articles.author: k.osei
articles.snippet: Threat actor dwelled 9 days using a CI build host excluded from EDR. Root cause: stale exclusion list. Contained pre-encryption.

body.p: T+0 initial access via exposed RDP on a contractor laptop. T+2d lateral movement to a Jenkins build host that had been added to the EDR exclusion list 'temporarily' 14 months prior. T+9d staging of encryptor detected by a canary file; contained before execution.
An EDR exclusion intended to fix a transient build-performance issue was never removed and never reviewed. The host became an unmonitored beachhead.
All EDR exclusions now expire after 30 days and require security sign-off to renew. Quarterly exclusion-list review added to the SOC SOP. RDP brokered exclusively through the bastion.

articles.title: Playbook: Business Email Compromise (BEC) response
articles.author: soc-team
articles.snippet: Step-by-step containment for confirmed BEC: revoke sessions, purge mailbox rules, rotate tokens, notify finance, preserve evidence.

body.p: Confirmed unauthorized access to a corporate mailbox, or a fraudulent wire request traced to an internal account.

1) Revoke all active sessions for the user. 2) Reset credentials and re-register MFA. 3) Enumerate and delete malicious inbox/forwarding rules. 4) Revoke OAuth grants for unrecognized apps. 5) Freeze any pending wire transfers via Finance.
Hunt for the same IOCs across all mailboxes. Review sign-in logs for the tenant. Restore mailbox rules from a known-good baseline. File a SAR if funds moved.

articles.title: Runbook: emergency out-of-band patch deployment
articles.author: platform-sec
articles.snippet: Compressed change process for actively-exploited CVEs: risk acceptance, phased rollout, rollback criteria, comms.

body.p: A CVE with CVSS ≥ 8.0 is under active exploitation AND an exploit is publicly available OR observed in your telemetry.
Emergency CAB approval (one VP + security lead). Phased rollout: 5% canary → 25% → 100% with 30-min soak gates. Predefined rollback if error budget breached.

articles.title: Identity & Access Management policy — privileged accounts
articles.author: grc-office
articles.snippet: Standards for privileged access: JIT elevation, phishing-resistant MFA, session recording, 90-day access reviews.

body.p: All accounts with administrative entitlements over production, identity, or security tooling.

Just-in-time elevation via PAM with a maximum 4-hour grant. Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2) mandatory. All privileged sessions recorded. Standing access prohibited except break-glass, which is monitored and alerts on use.
Entitlements recertified every 90 days by the resource owner. Orphaned accounts disabled within 24h of detection.

articles.title: NIST CSF 2.0 — control mapping & evidence index
articles.author: grc-office
articles.snippet: Crosswalk of internal controls to NIST CSF 2.0 functions (Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover) with evidence links.

body.p: Single source of truth mapping every internal control to NIST CSF 2.0 and SOC 2 trust criteria, with links to evidence artifacts for audit.
Govern 100%, Identify 94%, Protect 91%, Detect 88%, Respond 96%, Recover 82%. Gaps tracked in the GRC backlog with owners and due dates.

articles.title: Akira ransomware — SonicWall SSL-VPN exploitation cluster
articles.author: intel-pipeline
articles.snippet: Uptick in Akira intrusions via unpatched SonicWall SSL-VPN. Rapid encryption within 24-48h of access. Mitigations enclosed.

body.p: Multiple intrusions in the last 14 days share an initial-access vector: unpatched SonicWall SSL-VPN appliances lacking MFA. Time-to-ransom observed as short as 24 hours.
Patch SonicOS to the latest firmware, enforce MFA on all VPN logins, restrict VPN management interfaces from the public internet, and hunt for the IOCs below across firewall logs.
